# binney-turnkey-totalitarian-2012

- **URL:** https://www.wired.com/2012/03/ff-nsadatacenter/ (James Bamford, "The NSA Is Building the Country's Biggest Spy Center (Watch What You Say)," Wired, Mar. 15, 2012; full article text verified) · **Accessed:** 2026-08-25 · **For:** v1→v2 response round, exact wording and context of the "turnkey totalitarian state" remark
- **What it establishes:** The origin of the "turnkey" metaphor for latent surveillance capability, a year before Snowden: William Binney — former senior NSA crypto-mathematician, cofounder and chief of the agency's Signals Intelligence Automation Research Center, who resigned in late 2001 over the warrantless-wiretapping program — telling Bamford, apropos of Stellar Wind and the Utah Data Center, that the infrastructure for totalitarian control already exists and only awaits the turn of a key.
- **Key passages:** (verified verbatim against the Wired article text)
  - The quote in context: "Sitting in a restaurant not far from NSA headquarters, the place where he spent nearly 40 years of his life, Binney held his thumb and forefinger close together. 'We are, like, that far from a turnkey totalitarian state,' he says."
  - Note: the article ALSO carries a pull-quote variant without "like": "The former NSA official held his thumb and forefinger close together: 'We are that far from a turnkey totalitarian state.'" Both appear in the piece; the in-body narrative version includes ", like,".
  - Who Binney is (verbatim): "William Binney was a senior NSA crypto-mathematician largely responsible for automating the agency's worldwide eavesdropping network. … As chief and one of the two cofounders of the agency's Signals Intelligence Automation Research Center, Binney and his team designed much of the infrastructure that's still likely used to intercept international and foreign communications."
  - His resignation (verbatim): "Binney left the NSA in late 2001, shortly after the agency launched its warrantless-wiretapping program. 'They violated the Constitution setting it up,' he says bluntly. 'But they didn't care. They were going to do it anyway, and they were going to crucify anyone who stood in the way. When they started violating the Constitution, I couldn't stay.'"
  - Scale context (verbatim): asked how many communications the agency has intercepted since 9/11, "Binney estimates the number at 'between 15 and 20 trillion, the aggregate over 11 years.'"
- **Reliability:** Primary journalistic source for the quote (Bamford's first-on-the-record interview with Binney about Stellar Wind); Bamford is the leading independent chronicler of the NSA; Wired is a mainstream outlet. Binney is a named, on-the-record insider source.
- **Relevance to this project:** Bears on the latent-capability argument and the genealogy of the turnkey metaphor (this precedes Snowden's "turnkey tyranny" by ~15 months). If quoting, prefer the in-body version with attribution to Binney *as quoted by Bamford in Wired*, and preserve ", like," or use the pull-quote variant consistently.
